extracted.intended_audience: news organizations, journalists, and the general public interested in news trustworthiness
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for news organizations to demonstrate trustworthiness and transparency using The Trust Project's Trust Indicators; intended to help audiences assess whether a news story comes from a reliable source and to guide news organizations in best practices. Includes value statements and specific indicator commitments (e.g., disclosures, methods, corrections, diversity, engagement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful, verified news and information
rubrics_metrics.description: Truthful, verified news and information in a context that gives them meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes verification and providing context so information is meaningful to audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forums for civil exchanges and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Forums for civil exchanges and greater understanding of various viewpoints, with fairness in mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage civil public discussion and presentation of multiple viewpoints; fairness in moderation and framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stories reflecting diverse communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories, information and ideas that reflect diverse types of communities and their interests and views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage should include and reflect the interests and perspectives of different communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uphold the public interest and hold power accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Uphold the public’s interest, which includes holding the powerful accountable and shining a light in unexpected places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalism should serve public interest through watchdog reporting and investigative work that exposes wrongdoing or oversight failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete practice: publishing corrections or clarifications as promptly as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing corrections and clarifications promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing corrections or clarifications as promptly as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific corrective-procedure expectation tied to the fairness and accuracy commitment; implies active error acknowledgment and remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures about mission, funding, and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures that explain our mission, source(s) of funding and the organization behind us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make transparent who runs and funds the outlet; explain mission so audiences can evaluate potential biases or conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insight into methods and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Insight into our methods and where we get our information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information about reporting methods, sourcing and evidence so readers can judge rigor and provenance of facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: A diversity of voices and perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: A diversity of voices and perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively include multiple voices in reporting to present a fuller picture and avoid narrow or homogeneous perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunities for public engagement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer channels and mechanisms for audiences to participate, ask questions, provide feedback, and engage with reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display of the 8 Trust Indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust Project News Partners abide by the above principles and display the 8 Trust Indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The indicators are intended to 'show who and what is behind a news story so people can easily assess for themselves whether it comes from a reliable source'; displaying them is a visible signal of commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority (research- and evidence-based work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority: We base our work on research, evidence and the core ideals of journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should be grounded in evidence and established journalistic standards; sourcing and reasoning should support authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity (truthfulness and standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticity: We are truthful and follow strict standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitment to truthful presentation and adherence to internal editorial standards and ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency (openness and admitting mistakes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency: We are open, honest and accessible. We illuminate, not obfuscate, and admit our mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be candid about errors and processes; avoid hiding methods or motives; facilitate reader understanding of how reporting was done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusivity (center a diverse public)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusivity: Our work keeps a diverse public at its center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial planning and audience engagement should prioritize accessibility and relevance to varied demographic groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness (impartial and respectful)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairness: Our work is impartial and respectful of differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat subjects and audiences respectfully; present competing views without bias or disrespect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability (consistency and dependability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability: We are consistent – and can be counted on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent editorial practices and standards so audiences can depend on the outlet over time.
